notes.row_count_mismatch_investigation: First r10 training attempt used a naive glob (all shards in claude/n{29..32}-w{NN} branches as currently on origin) and got value=6085626/policy=1672686, NOT matching r7's 5966525/1624058. Root cause: branches n30-w06/w11/w15, n31-w03/w06/w16, n32-w06/w12 received additional part-shard pushes (_p2.._p7) to the SAME branch name after r7 had already fetched them (all part-shard commits dated 2026-09-11, before train-r7's 2026-09-12 04:56 commit) -- a moving-target branch, not a bug in my fetch. Killed that run before it finished/saved. Coordinator (via scheduled trigger) supplied the exact source dir list r7 actually used, extracted from nrel_r7.npz's meta['src']: wave31 excludes w03/w06 (aborted partials, only n31_w16_p2 included among part dirs), wave32 excludes w06/w12. Retrained with that exact list -- corpus fingerprint matched r7 exactly (value/policy rows AND aux valid-row count 2759667/5966525).
notes.export_effects_json_race: arena_shard's multiprocessing pool (4 workers) raced to regenerate opcg_sim/data/opcg_effects.json on first pool init (each worker's os.replace(tmp, out) stepping on another's), causing most workers to crash on the very first shard. Worked around by letting one successful run generate the cache file once, then restarting -- no code changes made. Not seen again after the cache existed.
notes.mirror_arena_deck_flag_bug_self_inflicte: First attempt at the mirror (fixed-leader) arena condition used --decks synth_roles, which crashed every pair (ValueError: not a leader: None) because opcg_sim/loop/decks.py leader_pair() returns (None, None) for --leaders fixed by design, and synth-style deck building requires a real leader id. The code's own docstring says the historical fixed-mirror band is measured with --decks singleton. Deleted the 8 void mirror shards (never committed) and reran with --decks singleton -- all 192 pairs completed void=0.
